answer: The solar apex (direction of the Sun's motion relative to nearby stars / local standard of rest) is in the constellation Hercules near Vega, at about R.A. 18h, Dec. +30 deg. Primary peer-reviewed determination Schönrich, Binney & Dehnen 2010 "Local Kinematics and the Local Standard of Rest": (U,V,W)sun = 11.1, 12.24, 7.25 km/s, i.e. total ~18 km/s. Summarized as: "toward which the Sun is moving with respect to the local standard of rest, at a rate of about 19.4 kilometers per second".

sources.contribution: The solar apex is the point on the celestial sphere, in the constellation Hercules at about R.A. 18h

We find U_sun = 11.1 km/s with respect to the local standard of rest
We find V_sun = 12.24 km/s with respect to the local standard of rest
We find W_sun = 7.25 km/s with respect to the local standard of rest

uncertainties: Schonrich et al. 2010 gives U,V,W components, not the constellation name Hercules explicitly; constellation comes from coordinate transformation / secondary summary
Total apex speed depends on LSR definition: ~18-19.4 km/s from U,V,W = 11.1, 12.24, 7.25 km/s vs older ~20 km/s and other modern ~13.4 km/s values using different V-component
